narrative:
The machine learning model predicted a 56.1% chance that you would fail the bar exam, which is a significant concern for your application to law school. This probability indicates that, based on the data analyzed, there is a greater likelihood of not passing the exam on your first attempt, which ultimately influenced the decision to deny your admission.

The most critical factors contributing to this prediction were your performance rankings in your third year and first year of studies, as well as your undergraduate GPA. Your rankings placed you in the lowest decile compared to accepted students, who typically performed much better. This suggests that your academic performance may not have met the expectations set by the law school for successful candidates. While your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 is above average, it was not enough to offset the concerns raised by your lower rankings.

In contrast, your LSAT score of 29.50 was significantly below the average of 37.18 among accepted students, which further pushed the prediction toward a higher likelihood of failure. This score is a critical indicator of readiness for the rigors of law school and the bar exam.

Moving forward, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your academic performance and preparing for the LSAT if you choose to reapply. Strengthening these areas could enhance your chances of success in future applications and on the bar exam.
